title: The Greys' faces traced onto their portraits and side views
items: William's moustache now falls only to the line of his mouth, so his lower lip shows, with a little bare skin under it before the beard begins; his beard's line runs up each cheek from the moustache's ends to the sideburns, as in his picture.

Sarah's face is traced onto her portrait and then onto the owner's square-on front view of her, where her cheeks show best: about 400 points of her face land within about a millimetre of the pictures'.

Both Greys' profiles are traced onto the side views of the owner's turnaround sheets: their noses are longer and stand further out, Sarah has her straight bridge and small chin, and the line under her jaw runs back to the throat as hers does.
William's nose is traced onto his portrait too, and both faces are now compared at the picture's own turn of the head, which had made his nose look as if it stood out.

Sarah's lips are thin, her nose tip level and her eyes blue-grey; William's hair falls in fuller waves to his collar, a brown going grey, and his grizzled beard lies close at the jaw and runs longer to the chin, as on the owner's sheets.
